The '''2007–08 [[La Liga]]''' season was the 77th since its establishment. It began on 25 August 2007, and concluded on 18 May 2008.

[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] secured a second consecutive La Liga title following a 2–1 victory over [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]] on 4 May 2008. This season, all European leagues ended earlier than the previous season, due to the impending [[UEFA Euro 2008]] tournament. It also was the first year of the new La Liga television agreement, which saw [[La Sexta]] mark its first year of television broadcasting.

This season was marred by the death of [[Antonio Puerta]], the player of [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], due to heart problems.

== Death of Antonio Puerta ==
On 25 August 2007, during started of season, [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] player [[Antonio Puerta]] collapsed and lost consciousness in the penalty area due to a cardiac arrest while on Sevilla's match against [[Getafe CF|Getafe]]. After recovering and being substituted, Puerta was able to walk to the dressing room, where he collapsed once again. He was resuscitated by the doctors and taken, by ambulance, to the [[intensive care unit]] of ''Virgen del Rocío'' hospital, where he received [[cardiopulmonary resuscitation]]. Later, Puerta dead on 28 August 2007 after suffering [[Multiple organ dysfunction syndrome|multiple organ failure]] and irreversible [[brain damage]] as a result of multiple prolonged cardiac arrests due to an incurable, [[Congenital Heart Disease|hereditary heart disease]] known as [[arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2007/08/28/actualidad/1188285718_850215.html|title=Muere Antonio Puerta|trans-title=Antonio Puerta dies|newspaper=[[El País]]|language=es|date=28 August 2007|access-date=8 January 2022}}</ref>

== Teams ==
Twenty teams competed in the league&nbsp;– the top seventeen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [[2006–07 Segunda División|Segunda División]]. The promoted teams were [[Real Valladolid|Valladolid]], [[UD Almería|Almería]], and [[Real Murcia|Murcia]]. Both Valladolid and Murcia returned to the top flight after a three-year absence while UD Almería were promoted for the first time. However, since AD Almería played in the [[1980–81 La Liga]], the city of Almería returned to the top fight after an absence of twenty six years. They replaced [[Celta de Vigo]], [[Real Sociedad]] and [[Gimnàstic de Tarragona|Gimnàstic]], ending their top flight spells of two, forty and one year respectively.

== Season statistics ==

=== Scoring ===
* '''First goal of the season''': [[Sergio Agüero]] for [[Atlético Madrid]] against [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] (25 August 2007)
* '''Fastest goal in a match''': '''7 seconds''' – [[Joseba Llorente]] for [[Real Valladolid|Valladolid]] against [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] (20 January 2008)
* '''Goal scored at the latest point in a match''': '''90+4 minutes'''
** [[Manu del Moral|Manu]] for [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] against [[Recreativo de Huelva|Recreativo]] (2 September 2007)
** [[Ebi Smolarek]] for [[Racing de Santander|Racing Santander]] against [[Recreativo de Huelva|Recreativo]] (23 March 2008)
** [[Roberto Ayala]] for [[Real Zaragoza|Zaragoza]] against [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo]] (3 May 2008)
* '''Widest winning margin''': 7 – [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] 7–0 [[Real Valladolid|Valladolid]] (10 February 2008)
* '''Most goals in a match''': 9 – [[Atlético Madrid]] 6–3 [[UD Almería|Almería]] (6 April 2008)
* '''First own goal of the season''': [[Daniel Jarque]] for [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] against [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] (25 September 2007)
* '''First hat-trick of the season''':
** {{flagicon|FRA|1974}} [[Thierry Henry]] for [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] against [[Levante UD|Levante]] (29 September 2007)
* '''Most goals in a match by one player''': '''3 goals'''
